slides.heading: Invert Binary Tree
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Binary Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Invert Binary Tree, a medium binary trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Mirror the tree by swapping every node's children.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Mirror the tree by swapping every node's children.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Swap every node's children, recursively or with a queue.
slides.narration: Swap every node's children, recursively or with a queue.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Every node must be swapped once → O(n) is optimal
Recursive (O(h) stack) or BFS queue (O(w) space)
slides.narration: Every node's children must be swapped, so linear time is optimal. Recursion uses stack space proportional to height; a breadth-first queue uses space proportional to the widest level. Order doesn't matter.

slides.heading: Approach
slides.narration: Step by step. First, visit each node. Second, swap left and right. Third, recurse into both children.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Swap children of 1
slides.narration: At node 1, swap its left and right children.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Swap children of 2
slides.narration: At node 2, swap its left and right children.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Swap children of 3
slides.narration: At node 3, swap its left and right children.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: If the node is null, return. Otherwise swap left and right with a temporary, then invert both subtrees.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of h.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Swap before or after recursion — both fine
slides.narration: Swapping a null child is fine. For very deep trees, prefer the iterative version.
